items.claim: The retrospective-colophon plus dated-reopening frame closing the Moab burden is byte-true at both cited verses, and this is the only row of the eight whose every pointed run survives re-collation at byte tier (2 of 2 runs at byte tier here, against 12 runs across the other seven rows reaching NFD only).
items.evidence: Both pointed runs re-collate against their cited refs at BYTE tier: the colophon quoted at oshb:Isa.16.13 opens זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר and closes מֵאָֽז, and the quote is the whole verse, so the self-naming retrospective frame is fully evidenced rather than gestured at; the reopening וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ stands verse-initial in the bytes of oshb:Isa.16.14, giving a genuine second frame onset on top of the colophon. The parashah disclosure is exact and complete: the mark inventory records a setumah (correctly typed, never conflated with petuchah) at oshb:Isa.16.14 and records no other mark inside oshb:Isa.16.13-Isa.16.14 (1 marked verse in the 2-verse span, out of 209 marked verses book-wide), so span-relevant symmetry is satisfied at tier-3, single witness, and the row's front-seam neighbour is unmarked so nothing further is owed. The closing seam is byte-clean: the verse-initial oracle header bounding this burden stands at oshb:Isa.15.1 and the next verse-initial header is oshb:Isa.17.1, so no header, woe cry, divine-speech frame or postpositive signature straddles oshb:Isa.16.14|Isa.17.1. Two residual observations, neither sufficient to overturn: the remnant-noun catchword וּשְׁאָ֥ר at oshb:Isa.16.14 recurs as וּשְׁאָ֣ר at oshb:Isa.17.3, but the pair is SKELETON tier only and byte-distinct in its accents, so it is a weak cohesion signal across the burden join rather than a byte-true device arguing continuity; and the rationale's closing clause reaches for pipeline structure instead of verse-anchored grounds, which is a register matter, not a byte matter.

items.claim: The oracle-header run that drives the row is labelled byte tier but re-collates only at NFD, and the English sentence the row calls the header's rendering is the line after the header, not the header.
items.evidence: The driving quote מַשָּׂ֖א דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק, cited at oshb:Isa.17.1 and self-labelled byte tier, re-collates at NFD tier ONLY: the combining marks have been canonically reordered against the source (source order shin, sin-dot, dagesh, qamats; quoted order shin, qamats, dagesh, sin-dot), the copy-degradation class that requires a re-splice from source bytes rather than a re-key. A false byte-tier label on the row's sole boundary driver is the defect; the underlying fact is sound, since the header does stand verse-initial in the bytes of oshb:Isa.17.1, and it is one of the ten verse-initial oracle headers of this series. The closing bracket verifies cleanly: נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת reaches BYTE tier and stands verse-final at oshb:Isa.17.3, and the only postpositive signature sites in this stretch are oshb:Isa.17.3, oshb:Isa.17.6 and oshb:Isa.19.4 (3 verses by inventory), so the bracket claim is not overstated. Second defect, quote/gloss parity: the row calls the sentence “Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.” (web:Isa.17.1) 'the WEB header', but the staged folded verse renders the Hebrew header as “The burden of Damascus.” (web:Isa.17.1) and the quoted sentence is the oracle's first line after it -- an English-side attribution the Hebrew does not carry. Mark disclosure is exact (setumah at oshb:Isa.16.14 and oshb:Isa.17.3, tier-3 single witness), and the paragraph-fold disclosure at the header matches the staged folded text, which the WEB quote is correctly measured against.

items.claim: Both pointed runs are labelled byte tier but re-collate only at NFD, and the row's own opening scene-turn run recurs BYTE-IDENTICALLY one verse past its closing seam with no disclosure.
items.evidence: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.17.4) and נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.17.6) each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY against their cited refs while both are self-labelled byte tier; the degradation is canonical reordering of combining marks (source bet, dagesh, patach against quoted bet, patach, dagesh). The substance of the closing bracket survives: the signature is verse-final in the bytes of oshb:Isa.17.6 and its wording is genuinely distinct from the one closing oshb:Isa.17.3 -- distinct divine titles, not a repeated formula. The undisclosed problem is cross-seam. The two-word run בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא carried inside this row's own opening formula is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the verse-initial run בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא standing one verse past the row's closing seam at oshb:Isa.17.7 -- identical to the accent, not merely to the consonants. That is a byte-true device straddling the row's own boundary and therefore arguing continuity against the cut, and it is nowhere disclosed; the rejected alternative instead reaches for shared subject matter, which is the weaker ground and leaves the strongest rival unnamed. Mark disclosure itself is exact and complete for the span (setumah at oshb:Isa.17.3 and oshb:Isa.17.6, tier-3 single witness, no interior mark omitted).

items.claim: The row's load-bearing recurrence claim is byte-false -- the two scene-turn runs it calls identical differ in their accents -- while the run that IS byte-identical sits across the row's own front seam and goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: The row asserts that its opening marker בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.17.7) recurs as 'the identical opening marker' at בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא (oshb:Isa.17.9), and labels both quotes byte tier. Re-collation contradicts both halves of that. First, each run reaches NFD tier ONLY against its cited ref, so neither byte-tier label holds. Second, and materially, the two runs are NOT byte-identical to each other: the oshb:Isa.17.7 run carries munach on the first word and zaqef qatan on the second, while the oshb:Isa.17.9 run carries qadma and geresh. Identity holds only at ACCENT-STRIPPED and SKELETON tier, and the row names no tier at all for the recurrence. This is not cosmetic: the row's internal no-cut argument -- that the aftermath continues as one row because the same marker recurs without an intervening closing signature -- rests precisely on that identity, so a tier the row never states is doing the work. Compounding it, the run that IS byte-identical to oshb:Isa.17.7 is בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא, inside the opening formula of oshb:Isa.17.4, i.e. across this row's own FRONT seam: the strongest byte-true rival to its opening cut is the one the row does not mention, while the weaker skeleton-tier recurrence inside the span is overstated as byte identity. The third quote קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל likewise re-collates at NFD only. Two things do verify: the divine-title site is genuine and is the sole title verse between oshb:Isa.12.6 and oshb:Isa.29.19 (25 title verses book-wide), and no postpositive signature falls anywhere inside oshb:Isa.17.7-Isa.17.11 (3 signature verses in oshb:Isa.15.1-Isa.21.17 by inventory -- oshb:Isa.17.3, oshb:Isa.17.6, oshb:Isa.19.4 -- none of them in this span), so the span itself is defensible even though its stated grounds are not.

items.claim: The row's single Hebrew run -- its only quoted boundary driver -- is labelled byte tier but re-collates at NFD; every other claim in the row verifies in the bytes.
items.evidence: ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים (oshb:Isa.17.12) re-collates at NFD tier ONLY against its cited ref while the row labels it byte tier, and it is the row's sole quoted Hebrew form, so the entire seam argument stands on a degraded copy and the row's Hebrew engagement is not at quotation grade. The challenge is confined to that. Everything else holds: the woe cry does stand verse-initial in the bytes of oshb:Isa.17.12; the row's claim that this unit carries no oracle header of its own is correct, since the verse-initial headers flanking it are oshb:Isa.17.1 and oshb:Isa.19.1 (10 verse-initial headers book-wide) and neither falls in the span; the closing seam is argued from the next woe cry ה֥וֹי אֶ֖רֶץ at oshb:Isa.18.1, which is disclosed rather than left silent, so the woe chain straddling oshb:Isa.17.14|Isa.18.1 is properly surfaced; and no postpositive signature falls inside oshb:Isa.17.12-Isa.17.14. Mark disclosure is exact and complete for the span (setumah at oshb:Isa.17.11 and oshb:Isa.17.14, tier-3 single witness), and the woe role is named as an onset rather than blended with the indictment, self-exclamation and invitation roles or with the separate woe lexeme.

items.claim: The row states the mid-span divine frame arrives without a fresh addressee shift, but the addressee marker sits inside the row's own quoted run and two further address turns precede it; all three pointed runs are labelled byte tier while re-collating at NFD.
items.evidence: The row's own quote כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.18.4) ends in the dative אֵלַ֔י, which names the prophet as the addressee of that frame -- so 'without a fresh addressee shift' is contradicted by the very bytes the row cites, and the frame is explicitly addressed rather than continuous with what precedes. Two further address turns stand immediately before it: the imperative address לְכ֣וּ מַלְאָכִ֣ים קַלִּ֗ים at oshb:Isa.18.2, and the universal vocative כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵ֖ל וְשֹׁ֣כְנֵי אָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Isa.18.3 closing on the second-person plural תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ. The row's own disclosed mid-span setumah falls at exactly oshb:Isa.18.3, so the tier-3 layer it discloses points at the rival cut its rejected alternative never considers -- that alternative weighs only a cut at the divine-speech onset, never the vocative. Separately, all three pointed runs -- the woe cry at oshb:Isa.18.1, and the frame and the doubled variant-note pair at oshb:Isa.18.4 -- re-collate at NFD tier ONLY against their cited refs while all three are self-labelled byte tier. The variant-note engagement is otherwise a real strength and should survive revision: the pair אשקוטה אֶשְׁקֳטָ֖ה does sit in the letter bytes of oshb:Isa.18.4 as a doubled token, the row correctly names which form is unpointed and which is pointed, the note inventory carries exactly one note there, and it is the only variant-note-bearing verse anywhere in oshb:Isa.16.13-Isa.19.15 (1 of 49 such verses book-wide). The frame is correctly owned as the divine one, not the royal-messenger class. Mark disclosure is exact and complete for the span (setumah at oshb:Isa.17.14, oshb:Isa.18.3 and oshb:Isa.18.7, tier-3 single witness).

items.claim: The oracle-header run driving the row is labelled byte tier but re-collates at NFD, and the English sentence set beside the header is the line after it rather than the header's own rendering.
items.evidence: מַשָּׂ֖א מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.19.1) re-collates at NFD tier ONLY against its cited ref despite the byte-tier label -- the same canonical-reordering degradation that runs through the neighbouring rows' quoted runs, and again it lands on the row's opening driver. The rest of the row verifies well. The closing signature נְאֻ֥ם הָאָד֖וֹן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת reaches BYTE tier and stands verse-final in the bytes of oshb:Isa.19.4; the stacked title form is named as the stacked form rather than folded into a bare divine-name count, which is the right count-object discipline; the header stands verse-initial in the bytes of oshb:Isa.19.1; and the claim that the following material is unbracketed is correct, since the only postpositive signature sites in this stretch are oshb:Isa.17.3, oshb:Isa.17.6 and oshb:Isa.19.4 (3 verses by inventory) and none falls after oshb:Isa.19.4 until well past the span. The secondary defect matches the other header row of this cluster: the staged folded verse renders the Hebrew header as “The burden of Egypt.” (web:Isa.19.1), while the row sets “Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.” (web:Isa.19.1) beside the header form -- so the English offered for the header is the line following it, a gloss-parity gap rather than a wrong seam. Mark disclosure is exact (setumah at oshb:Isa.18.7 on the front seam; the mark inventory records none inside oshb:Isa.19.1-Isa.19.4, and that absence is correctly left as no evidence either way), and the fold disclosure matches the staged folded text the WEB quote is measured against.

items.claim: The byform handling is genuinely right, but the comparison is drawn to a verse outside the span with no supporting ref while four in-span attestations go unmentioned, the cross-seam digit names neither swept object nor unit, and the pivot run is labelled byte tier while re-collating at NFD.
items.evidence: The strength first, because it should survive revision: יְאֹרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר (oshb:Isa.19.6) re-collates at BYTE tier, and the row is right to refuse to blend the poetic byform into an ordinary Egypt-name sweep. The hazard is real in this book -- a bare consonantal sweep on that skeleton returns 3 verses, one of which is מִצּ֖וּר at oshb:Isa.48.21, a rock-form with nothing to do with Egypt. But the row draws its contrast against 'this oracle's own header', i.e. oshb:Isa.19.1, a verse outside the span that appears nowhere in the row's evidence refs, while the ordinary Egypt name is attested in 4 verses INSIDE the span (oshb:Isa.19.12, oshb:Isa.19.13, oshb:Isa.19.14, oshb:Isa.19.15 -- e.g. מִצְרָֽיִם standing verse-final at oshb:Isa.19.12) and is never mentioned: the comparison was available in-span and was instead mirrored out of the span unsupported. Next, the closing cross-seam claim of a fivefold scene-turn series opening the following unit carries no swept object and no unit: the scene-turn phrase occurs in 6 verses of oshb:Isa.19.16-Isa.19.25 at skeleton tier, and reaches 5 only under an unstated verse-initial restriction that silently excludes the non-initial occurrence at oshb:Isa.19.21 -- a digit that names neither its object nor its unit and is wrong on the obvious reading. Third, the pivot quote אַךְ אֱוִלִים֙ (oshb:Isa.19.11) is labelled byte tier but re-collates at NFD only, though its verse-initial position in the bytes of oshb:Isa.19.11 is real. The no-internal-frame argument itself is sound and independently checks out: no oracle header, woe cry, divine-speech frame or postpositive signature falls anywhere in oshb:Isa.19.5-Isa.19.15. Mark disclosure is exact and complete for the span (setumah at oshb:Isa.19.15, tier-3 single witness, and the front-seam neighbour is unmarked so nothing further is owed).
